summary:
✅ Risk Score: LOW (20/100)

1 High · 1 Medium

Review completed with 2 findings across 2 agents (1 high, 1 medium).

⚠️ 1 critical/high severity issues require immediate attention:
  - [HIGH] Unescaped user input in log message reintroduces log-injection (CVE-2026-111211 regression) (LogicAgent)

findings.title: Unescaped user input in log message reintroduces log-injection (CVE-2026-111211 regression)
findings.description: The user-supplied `value` is interpolated into the log message without escaping control characters (newlines, carriage returns, ANSI escape sequences). Python's `logging` module does not sanitize `%s` arguments, so a submitted geometry string like `"POINT(0 0)\n2025-01-01 00:00:00 ERROR Admin logged in"` will produce a multi-line log entry that appears to be a separate, forged log record. This is the exact behavior the removed `log_message()` helper (from `django.utils.log`) was designed to prevent — it escaped non-printable characters via `\x`/`\U` notation. The diff also removes the corresponding tests (`test_deserialize_logs_escaped_value`) that verified this escaping, and removes the CVE-2026-111211 entries from three release-note files, confirming this is a regression of a previously shipped security fix.
findings.suggestion:
Restore the use of `django.utils.log.log_message` (or at minimum apply `django.utils.text.trim_value` plus manual escaping of control characters) so that user-supplied values are escaped before being written to the log. Example:

```python
from django.utils.log import log_message
from django.utils.text import trim_value

trimmed, suffix = trim_value(value)
log_message(
    logger,
    "Error creating geometry from value '%s' + suffix + " (%s)",
    trimmed,
    err,
    level="error",
)
```

findings.title: Log injection regression: unescaped user-controlled geometry value written to logs (reverts CVE-2026-111211 fix)
findings.description: The diff reverts the fix for CVE-2026-111211. The `value` parameter is user-controlled form input (submitted via `GeometryField` widgets). Previously, `log_message()` from `django.utils.log` was used, which escapes control characters (newlines, ANSI escape sequences, Unicode) before writing to the log. The new code passes the raw `value` directly to `logger.error()`, allowing an attacker to inject control characters into application logs. For example, submitting a geometry value containing `\n` or `\x1b[31m` will write those bytes unescaped into log output, enabling log forgery, manipulation of log structure, and potential hiding of malicious activity from log-based monitoring/alerting systems. The `trim_value()` call is also removed, so arbitrarily large user input (e.g., a 10 MB string) will be logged in full, creating a minor log-flooding vector.
findings.suggestion:
Restore the use of `django.utils.log.log_message()` and `django.utils.text.trim_value()` to escape control characters and cap the logged value length:

```python
from django.utils.log import log_message
from django.utils.text import trim_value

# In the except block:
trimmed, suffix = trim_value(value)
log_message(
    logger,
    "Error creating geometry from value '%s" + suffix + "' (%s)",
    trimmed,
    err,
    level="error",
)
```

Also restore the corresponding tests (`test_deserialize_logs_escaped_value` and `test_deserialize_logs_trimmed_value`) and the CVE documentation in release notes to prevent future regressions.
